final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not curative. The admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout controls and monitoring exist. It also supports that the HR benefits enrollment segment is below target, remains exposed in rollout, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. The governing policy requires disclosure for a material limitation in a named launch use case unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text separately states that rollout controls do not remove that duty when exposure remains. A qualified path to launch may exist in principle if pre-launch disclosure is actually evidenced, but the current record identifies disclosure as necessary rather than proving it occurred. That distinction keeps the present certification basis evidentially incomplete, so `compliant_with_caveats` is not yet supported on this record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the HR benefits enrollment limitation has been completed or approved.
No approved risk acceptance specific to the exposed HR benefits enrollment segment is in the record.
The affected HR benefits enrollment use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
